{{nihongo|'''Kudo Shrine'''|久度神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Ōji, Nara|Q1346392|qid=Q1346392}}, {{ill|Kitakatsuragi District, Nara|Q1131013|qid=Q1131013}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. {{nihongo|'''Kudo Shrine'''|久度神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank in the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system#shosha}} was village shrine. In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Diet Library Digital Collection |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1273537/1/44 |website=dl.ndl.go.jp |access-date=2024-02-05}}</ref>, it is written as “Kudono Shrine” (クトノジンジャ).

== Overview ==
The ''{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}'' says that in {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 2 (783), it was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=official shrine}} and granted the divine rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. It is also listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} as “Kudo no Kami, {{ill|Heguri district|Q11483501|qid=Q11483501}}, {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}}.”

Also, at the second seat of {{ill|Hirano Shrine|Q738971|qid=Q738971}} (former {{ill|Q712534|lt=kanpei taisha}}) in Kita Ward, of the {{ill|Juan Bautista Massa|Q1389395|qid=Q1389395}} in Enryaku 13 (794), Kudo-no-Kami was enshrined after being transferred from this shrine<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.kamnavi.jp/as/ikoma/kudo.htm |title=[Kannabi] Kudo Shrine |access-date=2022-12-17}}</ref>.

The enshrined deities are Kudo Ōkami, {{ill|Hachiman|ar|هاتشيمان|az|Haçiman|ca|Hachiman|de|Hachiman|el|Χατσίμαν|es|Hachiman|eu|Hachiman|fa|هاچیمان|fi|Hachiman|fr|Hachiman|hu|Hacsiman|id|Hachiman|it|Hachiman|ja|八幡神|ko|하치만 신|mni|ꯍꯆꯤꯃꯥꯟ|my|ဟချိမန်း|pl|Hachiman|pt|Hachiman|ru|Хатиман|simple|Hachiman|sl|Hačiman|sv|Hachiman|tok|jan sewi Kasiman|tr|Hachiman|uk|Хачіман|uz|Hachiman|vi|Hachiman|wuu|八幡神|zh|八幡神|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman Ōkami}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|lt=Sumiyoshi Ōkami|qid=Q1114013}}, and {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|fr|Kasuga no Kami|ja|春日神|simple|Kasuga-no-Kami|zh|春日神|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasuga Ōkami}}<ref>Shrine notice board</ref>.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ''{{ill|jinjameisaichou|Q11590704|qid=Q11590704}}'', “Kudo-no-Kami” was not recorded, but in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 43, Kudo-no-Kami was invited from Hirano Shrine (former kanpei taisha) and enshrined in the main sanctuary of Kudo Shrine, the original seat.

Kudo Ōkami is a {{ill|Kitchen God|lt=kitchen hearth deity|qid=Q249178}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hirano Shrine|url=https://www.hiranojinja.com/home/gaiyo|access-date=2025-10-26}}</ref>.

Kudo Ōkami was conferred Senior First Rank in {{ill|Eihō|Q1193881|qid=Q1193881}} 1 ({{ill|1081|Q19450|qid=Q19450}})<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nara Prefecture Jinja-chō: Kudo Shrine|url=https://jinja-net.jp/jinjacho-nara/jsearch3nara.php?jinjya=5810|access-date=2025-10-29}}</ref>.

The oldest stone lantern at the shrine is from {{ill|Ryakuō|Q1146182|qid=Q1146182}} 1 (1338) in the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012}}, and a {{ill|Kasuga Mandalas|Q11513629|qid=Q11513629}} with a box inscription from {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} 8 (1476) is deposited at {{ill|Nara National Museum|Q147312|qid=Q147312}}<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.oji.nara.jp/kakuka/chiikiseibi/chiikikoryu/ojicyorekishishiryoshitsu/ojibunkazai/148.html |title=Kudo Shrine / Ōji Town |access-date=2022-12-22 |publisher=Ōji Town}}</ref>.

== Access ==
About 10 minutes on foot west of the north side of {{ill|Ōji Station (Nara)|Q856582|qid=Q856582}} ({{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125}} and {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085}}).
